newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Telecom says Argentina revises phone rates.
newsitem.headline: Telecom says Argentina revises phone rates.

text.p: Telecom Argentina said Thursday the government had set reductions in long-distance telephone call rates and increased tariffs for local calls.
The company said in a statement that neither it nor the other privatized telecommunications company, Telefonica de Argentina, stood to make any profit out of the revision of call tariffs.

Telecom and Telefonica, who replaced the state telephone company ENTEL in a 1991 privatization carried out by Peronist President Carlos Menem, have long been lobbying for a revision of the tariff structure.
They argued that reduced long-distance rates in Argentina and lower international rates would make charges fairer and reduce costs for businesses, especially in the provinces.
But consumer groups argued that private users' phone bills would rise and phone companies would pocket the difference.
Telecom said in Thursday's statement that the new tariffs "will facilitate the creation of a competitive scenario in the telecommunications sector."
It added that the new rules meant any extra tariff income resulting from the revised call rate structure would have to be ploughed back into further reductions in call rates.

Talk that such a deal was imminent boosted Argentine telecommunications shares late in Thursday trading, dealers said. Telecom shares in Buenos Aires closed $0.15 higher at $4.50 and Telefonica was also up $0.15 at $2.92.
Both stocks had also seen broker upgrades Thursday.

Telecom said long-distance calls of up to 110 km will be cut to $0.24 a minute from $0.32, calls of up to 240 km fall to $0.47 from $0.70 and the rate for longer distance calls is chopped by 56 percent to $0.61.
"That means a call from Buenos Aires to Cordoba has the same tariff as one from Buenos Aires to Salta," it said.
International call rates fall an average of 42 percent. Calls to the United States drop to $0.90 from $2.24 and for Germany, for example, the average charge will fall to $1.50 a minute from $4.08.
There is a new single tariff for calls to Argentina's Mercosur partners Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay. For example, the average daytime call to Brazil will now fall 48 percent in price to $0.90.
For urban calls, the rate for the 10am to 1pm peak time is increased to $0.03 from $0.02. Non-peak daytime call charges are unchanged at $0.022.
